name: Lagrange's Theorem
original_full_statement: For any finite group G, the order of every subgroup H of G divides the order of G.
hypotheses: H is a subgroup of G
conclusion: The order of H divides the order of G.

name: Cauchy's Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a finite group and p is a prime number dividing the order of G, then G contains an element of order p.
hypotheses: p divides the order of G
conclusion: There exists an element x in G such that the order of x is p.

name: Index Two Subgroup Theorem
original_full_statement: Every subgroup of index 2 in a group G is a normal subgroup of G.
hypotheses: H is a subgroup of G
The index of H in G is 2
conclusion: H is a normal subgroup of G.

name: Finite Integral Domains
original_full_statement: Every finite integral domain is a field.
hypotheses: R contains a finite number of elements
conclusion: R is a field.

name: First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings
original_full_statement: Let f: R -> S be a ring homomorphism. Then the kernel of f is an ideal of R, and the image of f is isomorphic to R/ker(f).
hypotheses: f is a ring homomorphism from R to S
conclusion: The quotient ring R/ker(f) is isomorphic to the image f(R).

name: Eisenstein's Criterion
original_full_statement: Let f(x) = a_n x^n + ... + a_0 be a polynomial with integer coefficients. If there exists a prime p such that p divides a_i for i < n, p does not divide a_n, and p^2 does not divide a_0, then f(x) is irreducible over the rational numbers.
hypotheses: f(x) is a polynomial in Z[x] of degree n > 0
p divides a_i for all i from 0 up to n-1
conclusion: f(x) is irreducible over the field of rational numbers Q.

name: Euler's Totient Theorem
original_full_statement: If n and a are coprime positive integers, then a raised to the power of the totient of n is congruent to 1 modulo n.
hypotheses: The greatest common divisor of a and n is 1
conclusion: a^phi(n) is congruent to 1 modulo n.

name: Euclid's Lemma
original_full_statement: If a prime p divides the product ab of two integers a and b, then p must divide at least one of a and b.
conclusion: p divides a or p divides b.

name: Wilson's Theorem
original_full_statement: A natural number n > 1 is a prime number if and only if (n-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo n.
hypotheses: n is a natural number greater than 1
conclusion: (n-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo n.

name: Cyclicity of the Multiplicative Group of a Finite Field
original_full_statement: The multiplicative group of any finite field is cyclic.
hypotheses: F has a finite number of elements
conclusion: The group of non-zero elements of F under multiplication is a cyclic group.

name: Cayley's Theorem
original_full_statement: Every group G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group acting on G.
conclusion: G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group Sym(G)

name: Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem
original_full_statement: Let G be a finite group acting on a set X. For any x in X, the size of the orbit of x multiplied by the size of the stabilizer of x equals the order of G.
hypotheses: G acts on a set X
x is an element of X
conclusion: |G| = |Orb(x)| * |Stab(x)|

name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Rings
original_full_statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity, and let I_1, ..., I_k be ideals such that I_i + I_j = R for all i != j. Then the map from R to the product of quotients R/I_i is surjective with kernel equal to the intersection of the ideals.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with identity
I_1, I_2, ..., I_k are ideals of R
I_i + I_j = R for all i != j

name: Characterization of Prime Ideals
original_full_statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity. An ideal P of R is prime if and only if the quotient ring R/P is an integral domain.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with identity
P is a proper ideal of R
conclusion: P is a prime ideal if and only if R/P is an integral domain

name: Primitive Element Theorem
original_full_statement: Every finite separable field extension L/K is a simple extension.
hypotheses: L/K is a finite field extension
conclusion: There exists an element α in L such that L = K(α)

name: Tower Law for Field Extensions
original_full_statement: If L is a finite extension of K and M is a finite extension of L, then M is a finite extension of K and [M:K] = [M:L][L:K].
hypotheses: K, L, and M are fields such that K ⊆ L ⊆ M

name: Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
original_full_statement: For distinct odd primes p and q, the Legendre symbol (p/q) times (q/p) equals (-1) raised to the power ((p-1)/2 * (q-1)/2).

name: Third Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
original_full_statement: Let G be a group, and let N and H be normal subgroups of G with N contained in H. Then (G/N)/(H/N) is isomorphic to G/H.
hypotheses: N is a normal subgroup of G
H is a normal subgroup of G
N is a subgroup of H
conclusion: (G/N) / (H/N) ≅ G/H

name: Hilbert's Basis Theorem
original_full_statement: If R is a Noetherian ring, then the polynomial ring R[x] is also a Noetherian ring.
conclusion: The polynomial ring R[x] is a Noetherian ring

name: Fermat's Theorem on Sums of Two Squares
original_full_statement: An odd prime p can be expressed as a sum of two squares x^2 + y^2 for integers x and y if and only if p is congruent to 1 modulo 4.
conclusion: p = x^2 + y^2 for some integers x, y if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod 4)

name: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
original_full_statement: Every integer n > 1 can be represented as a product of prime numbers in a unique way, up to the order of the factors.
conclusion: n can be uniquely factored into a product of primes, up to the order of the factors.

name: Bézout's Identity
original_full_statement: Let a and b be integers with greatest common divisor d. Then there exist integers x and y such that ax + by = d.
hypotheses: d is the greatest common divisor of a and b
conclusion: There exist integers x and y such that ax + by = d.

name: Second Isomorphism Theorem for Groups
original_full_statement: If H is a subgroup of G and N is a normal subgroup of G, then (H ∩ N) is a normal subgroup of H and H/(H ∩ N) ≅ HN/N.
hypotheses: H is a subgroup of G
N is a normal subgroup of G
conclusion: H/(H ∩ N) is isomorphic to HN/N.

name: Center of a p-group Theorem
original_full_statement: If G is a finite group of prime power order p^n for n > 0, then the center of G is non-trivial.
hypotheses: The order of G is p^n for some integer n ≥ 1
conclusion: The center Z(G) of G has order greater than 1.

name: Correspondence Theorem for Groups
original_full_statement: Let N be a normal subgroup of G. There is a bijection between the set of subgroups of G containing N and the set of subgroups of G/N.
hypotheses: N is a normal subgroup of G
conclusion: There exists a bijection between the set of subgroups of G that contain N and the set of subgroups of the quotient group G/N.

name: Characteristic of an Integral Domain
original_full_statement: The characteristic of any integral domain is either 0 or a prime number p.
conclusion: The characteristic of D is either 0 or a prime number p.

name: Freshman's Dream
original_full_statement: In a commutative ring of prime characteristic p, (x + y)^p = x^p + y^p for all elements x and y.
hypotheses: The characteristic of R is a prime number p
conclusion: For all x, y ∈ R, (x + y)^p = x^p + y^p.

name: Ideal Characterization of Fields
original_full_statement: A commutative ring R with identity 1 ≠ 0 is a field if and only if its only ideals are {0} and R.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring with multiplicative identity 1 ≠ 0
conclusion: R is a field if and only if the only ideals of R are the zero ideal and the ring itself.

name: Finiteness Implies Algebraicity
original_full_statement: Every finite field extension is an algebraic extension.
hypotheses: The degree of the extension [L:K] is finite
conclusion: Every element α ∈ L is algebraic over K.

name: Existence of Splitting Fields
original_full_statement: For any field K and any non-constant polynomial f(x) in K[x], there exists a splitting field for f(x) over K.
hypotheses: f(x) is a polynomial in K[x] of degree n ≥ 1
conclusion: There exists an extension field E of K such that f(x) factors into linear factors in E[x].
